title: Haymaker Tussle
pitch: Run like a human bumper car, build momentum, and punch up to 14 rivals off a shrinking floating arena until one is left.
core_loop: Wait in the lobby and practise movement and punching
Spawn on the arena and build momentum
Punch rivals to raise their stagger and launch them off the edge
Survive as the arena shrinks until one player is left
Return to the lobby for the next round
win_condition: Be the last player on the arena. If the last players go out together, the round announces no winner and restarts (editable default).
lose_condition: Fall off the arena or leave the play area. There is no health and no time limit.
out_of_scope: abilities, combos or dodges beyond the alternating punch and the shared propel

systems.name: KnockbackService

systems.name: TrainingService

systems.name: MovementController

systems.name: CombatController
systems.owns: Punch input, one request per press, and combat feedback shown from server results

systems.name: AnimationController

systems.name: HudController

systems.name: DummyService

systems.owns: Relaying propeles to other players, with its own cooldown

decisions.kick: USER REQUEST 2026-11-04: a shared skill on Space, gamepad Y or a touch button. Leap up, hang and aim a ring on the floor, front flip at it, then kick down. A small quick-time ring grades the second press; the server does the grading. The user's comic picture is the reference only for the round front flip, nothing else from it. The server decides every hit.
decisions.stagger_timing: A punch uses the target's stagger from before that hit, then adds to it. The first punch on a fresh player is always the same strength, which makes hits easy to read.
decisions.network_model: Each client owns and simulates its own character for responsiveness. The server never trusts a reported speed: it measures position over time and caps the result (Security settings).
decisions.knockback: The server decides knockback and the owning client applies it, per the vault's Combat Systems Architecture note. Trade-off: a cheating client could ignore it; to be checked in step 3.
decisions.player_collisions: Players do not solid-collide with each other. The server detects two players closing fast and knocks both along the line they collided on. USER 2026-11-03, replacing an equal split asked for earlier the same day: whoever was driving faster along that line recoils less and keeps some speed, the other is shoved further and loses theirs, which gives the faster runner a chance to punish with a punch. Always weaker than a punch; an even head-on splits evenly. Solid collisions between client-owned characters are the known route to accidental launches and fling exploits. To be judged by feel in step 3. USER 2026-11-04, replacing the rules before: a bump is two punches at once, for both sides, with real knockback and stagger; the faster one makes the other stagger a little more, and the difference stays small.
decisions.final_stage: The arena keeps shrinking to radius 0, so no safe minimum exists. Below FinalStageRadius it never pauses and every remaining player must eventually fall.
decisions.no_survivor: Eliminations are batched. If a batch removes every remaining player, nobody is picked by list order: the game announces no winner and restarts.
decisions.no_meshes_stage: Removed the mesh stage: the brief asks for simple geometry and placeholder materials, so no asset is planned for it.
decisions.propel: USER DECISION 2026-11-03, overrides the brief's 'no dodge ability or swerve cooldown': every player gets the same ability, Q or gamepad B or a touch button. It began as a dash. USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 replaced that with a propel, using a Red Bull drift video as the reference: a burst of speed along travel during which turning makes a car-style drift, with the body angled into the turn while travel slides wide and smoke trails. It never goes backward. Normal running keeps its sharp grip; the drift happens only during a propel.
decisions.propel_security: The propel runs on the owning client, like all movement. The combat step must make the server measure it too: SpeedTrustCap already stops a propel raising punch strength beyond the cap, and the speed check must allow for propeles.
decisions.lag_compensation: Punches are decided on the server at impact, with targets rewound by the attacker's ping, capped at MaxRewindSeconds. The vault lists a server decision with no rewind as a mistake. Only targets rewind.
decisions.test_bot: USER 2026-11-05: the attacking test bot is back, on the 1v1 arena only, after being removed for the training arena earlier the same day. It exists only when exactly one player is in the server, chases and punches like a player on the same movement and punch rules, has a slower punch and a reaction delay so it can be out-played, and doesn't propel. TestBot.Fights false makes it stand still. Training dummies stay passive: only the bot's spec has a brain. Its brain was rebuilt from its settings, not restored.
decisions.tutorial_repeats: Nothing persists (no datastore in scope), so the tutorial shows on every join rather than only the first. Showing it once per person needs saved data, which is the user's call.
decisions.wind_look: USER 2026-11-03: propel shows a gust on both sides of the feet that fades, inspired by the user's propel-puff picture, not copied. The user's message also called it what combat should look like, so hits use the same style. Built from pooled, decorative parts instead of a harvested particle pack, because the user asked for this specific look.
decisions.training_arena: USER 2026-11-05: a dedicated training arena beside the 1v1 arena with stations for M1s, uppercut and kick, stagger comparison, close range and hitboxes, a moving target and offstage recovery. Dummies use the real combat rules and stay out of competitive lists.
decisions.rounds: USER 2026-11-09: the game is a full arena of 30 fighters. When only a few real players are on (5 to 9), bots fill each round up to 20 fighters, and bots fight anyone, players or bots (bot fill is round piece 2). A lobby holds the training area; when a round starts everyone is teleported onto the arena, except players who pressed the AFK button, who sit it out. Ring-out credit goes to whoever last punched, kicked, bumped or clashed them within 4 s (Round.CreditSeconds); otherwise they fell on their own. Until the lobby exists, the training area is the lobby: new, waiting and eliminated players are there. In Studio the single test bot counts as a fighter so a round can be tested alone (Round.StudioBotCounts). The arena grew from radius 75 to 105 for 30 fighters (the same space each), with 30 spawn points; its look will be redone from the user's reference image.
decisions.max_players_25: USER 2026-11-10: the full arena is 25 fighters, not 30 (supersedes the 30 in 'rounds'). The arena keeps the same room per fighter as the original 15-player arena (pi*75^2/15 = 1178 square studs each), so 25 need about 29,450: StartRadius 97 (was 105), SpawnRadius 67 (was 73, the same share of the radius), SpawnCount 25. The Blender maps keep their oval's 115:95 shape at the same area: semi-axes 106.5 x 88 (was 115 x 95), design/maps/common.py.
decisions.gnomon_rework_b: USER 2026-11-10 (Gnomon only): double the arena's length and width ONCE (original oval 213 x 176 studs, semi-axes 106.5 x 88; now 426 x 352, semi-axes 213 x 176, recorded as absolute numbers in MapEnvironments.gnomon.arena and design/maps/common.py OVALS so a rerun can't double it again); grow the island to fit; no 3D grass or painted blades: the ground is shade 9 of the user's matcha reference (a very deep forest green, about sRGB 12,25,7 sampled), solid and matte; a few colliding obstacles (rocks plus tree stumps, design/maps/obstacles.py -> Config/MapObstacles.luau, round upright Cylinder colliders); fix scenery clipping and the hot-air balloons (pieces must move together); keep the lobby's view of the arena clear. Ring-out and spawns follow the live map's oval (Round.arenaFor, ActiveArena). The lobby moved out and up to stay past the bigger arena's out line and see its floor: Lobby.ViewEdgeZ 170 -> 250, SpawnZ 312 -> 266 (16 from the edge), FloorY 101 -> 111 (the most the eye-height rule Lobby.seesNearEdge allows with the spawn that close: higher, or a deeper spawn, and the lobby's own edge hides the arena's near edge). Fill bots wait in rows behind the spawn, not along the viewing edge. The map changes only when the next round starts (MapService.ChangeForNextRound).
decisions.pond_slowdown: USER 2026-11-11: one shallow pond in the middle of Gnomon's battlefield; wading in it slows you moderately (Pond.SpeedMultiplier, adjustable), clearing promptly when you step out (Pond.Ease per second), never stacking or outliving a death (it is worked out from where the body is, every frame, not stored). It multiplies with stagger and every other speed rule. The shape (MapEnvironments.gnomon.pond) is the same formula the Blender build carves the basin with (design/maps/gnomon_dress.py).
decisions.bot_fill_test: USER 2026-11-10: fill rounds with bots to simulate a full game (24 bots + the player = 25). Round.BotFill is the total a round is filled up to with bots (0 = off); Round.BotFillStudioOnly keeps it to Studio until the real rule (bots only when few players are on) is built. Fill bots wait along the lobby's viewing edge, fight the nearest fighter in the round (player or bot) with the test bot's brain, and are removed when knocked out or when the round ends. UPDATE 2026-11-10 (user, for Team Test): BotFillStudioOnly is false, so bots fill on any server and one real player can start a round; the test bot counts too. Turn BotFillStudioOnly back on (or build the real few-players rule) before the game goes public.

plan.overview: Haymaker Tussle. Round-based PvP ring-out brawler, up to 15 players, for PC, phone, tablet and gamepad. Target age is not set by the brief; content is cartoon punching with no blood or damage numbers.
plan.pitch_and_usp: A human bumper-car brawl: momentum is the weapon. Unlike glove-collecting slap games, everyone has one identical punch, and speed plus stagger decide how far it launches.
plan.core_concept: 0 min: run, feel the coasting, punch a dummy. 5 min: curve around rivals and hit at speed. 30 min: pick fights near the edge and time the shrink. Tomorrow: nothing persists in this prototype, so returning relies only on the fun of the fight.
plan.player_experience: Exaggerated, chaotic and weighty but controllable. The first win lands within seconds, when a first punch visibly shoves someone in training or at the round's start.
plan.audience: Casual and social players who want quick, funny fights with friends; easy to read, with skill in steering and timing.
plan.market: Slap Battles is the closest Roblox game: gloves and abilities, knock rivals off platforms. Sources found were low-quality pages, so treat those details as unverified. Super Smash Bros is the model for damage raising launch distance (SmashWiki). This game's gap is one shared move with momentum as the depth. Roblox DevForum threads confirm client-owned characters can fling others through collisions. See design/Research Notes.md.
plan.mechanics: Momentum steering with arcs and coasting; one shared propel; one alternating punch; speed and stagger-scaled knockback; small bumps; shrinking arena; last survivor wins; lobby and training with dummies. No economy.

progression.declined: Brief's first version has rounds only; nothing carries between rounds.

plan.content: One arena with 15 spawns, one lobby, one training area with 3 dummies. No enemies, items or collectibles.
plan.world: Arena: floating circle for the round, shrinks to nothing. Lobby: safe floor where punches animate but do nothing. Training area: marked zone in the lobby where punches work between eligible players and dummies.

story.declined: A brawl needs no story; the brief defines none.

plan.ui_ux: One HUD: round state, countdowns, survivors, speed, own stagger, punch cooldown, instructions, shrink warning, training status, result banner. Stagger bars over opponents. Mobile punch button. Punching is one press. No round timer.
plan.tutorial: USER 2026-11-03, replacing no forced tutorial: a skippable tutorial on every join, because nothing saves yet. Five steps taught by doing: run to the dummy, punch on the live CLICK NOW prompt (3 hits), hit at speed, bump then punish, propel. The prompt uses the server's hitbox rule at the moment a punch would land. USER 2026-11-03: it is mainly for practising on other players. The target is the nearest other player, or the test bot when alone. The bot stays calm until the tutorial ends. For now it runs on the test floor; it moves to the training area with the lobby step.
plan.art_direction: Prototype look: simple geometry, placeholder materials, a strong clear edge and readable ground rings. Characters are players' own R6 avatars. All animation follows the top-heavy, wide-armed energy of the reference.
plan.audio: SFX roles: punch swing, punch hit, bump, launch, elimination, shrink warning, countdown tick, round start and victory. Lobby and fight music are optional and only if a suitable track is found.
plan.technical_architecture: Rojo project with Knit services and controllers and plain RemoteEvents. Pure rules (knockback, stagger, shrink, punch checks) live in shared Core modules with headless Lune tests. All tunables come from GameConfig, generated from design/game.json.

data_saving.declined: Nothing persists in the first version, so there is no datastore.

plan.security: The server owns round state, cooldowns, impact timing, hit checks, stagger, knockback, training eligibility and results. Clients send only a punch intent, with no targets or strength. Remotes are rate limited, and malformed or non-finite values are dropped. Speed is measured by the server and capped.
plan.multiplayer: Up to 15 per round. Disconnects, deaths and resets count as eliminations with accurate counts. Late joiners and respawned players wait in the lobby. A countdown cancels if too few players remain.

monetisation.declined: Not in the brief; first version is the core loop only.

economy.declined: No currency in the first version.

retention.declined: No progression or rewards in the first version; test whether the fight is fun alone first.

social.declined: No parties, trading or leaderboards in the first version. Sparring in training is the only social feature.
